newsitem.title: FRANCE: France may attract less investment - Daewoo boss.
newsitem.headline: France may attract less investment - Daewoo boss.

text.p: France may become less attractive to foreign investors if the new Socialist government adopts policies to create 700,000 jobs and cut working weeks without reducing wages, the chairman of Daewoo Electronics was quoted as saying in the French newspaper Les Echos.

It said chairman Soon Hoon Bae, whose group has been keen to buy the Thomson Multimedia (TMM) arm of the state-owned Thomson group, told a foreign relations institute that high labour costs could mean job losses.

"If the government reduces the work-week to 35 hours a week (without lowering wages), we'll have to evaluate the cost. No doubt it will rise between 10 and 12 percent. If we cannot match that in productivity gains, we will have a problem," he said.
"Labour costs that are too high will result in job losses for France," he added.

Soon Hoon Bae had recently reiterated the group's interest in TMM -- whose sale proposed by the previous conservative government was scrapped after an Independent Commission opposed the terms -- but he appeared to have grown more cautious.
He said he needed information on new Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's plans for TMM before deciding whether Daewoo was still interested.
The change in government has raised doubts about the entire privatisation programme.

He saw two possible strategies to restore TMM's profitability. The first was short-term action involving job cuts, which he said did not appear to be in line with the left's policies and which also offered no guarantee that TMM would become more competitive against Sony and Philips.
The second was a strategic policy to enable TMM to develop on other markets that would require heavy funding, he said.
TMM reported a 3.1 billion franc loss for 1996.
